about:
Hi, I'm Sarah!

Designer, developer, artist, coach, and lifelong learner.

I'm Sarah Kostuk, a creative and detail-oriented designer based in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan. I'm passionate about bringing together technology, creativity, and problem-solving to develop meaningful, functional, and user-friendly digital experiences. 
My interests span software development, interactive systems design, programming, user experience, graphic design, and digital art. I enjoy exploring how different disciplines connect and how thoughtful design can make information more accessible, experiences more enjoyable, and ideas easier to communicate.
Whether I'm creating digital artwork, designing a website, developing an application, or organizing a softball practice, I draw on the same combination of creativity, analytical thinking, organization, and problem-solving. My background in computer science helps me approach challenges logically, while my experience with design thinking allows me to be efficient and creative and consider different perspectives. Coaching has strengthened my ability to communicate ideas, adapt to different needs, and turn plans into action. Together, these skills shape how I approach every project, from identifying a problem and exploring possible solutions to experimenting, and refining ideas.

My Education

I'm a fourth-year student at the University of Saskatchewan, pursuing degrees in Interactive Systems Design and Studio Art, along with minors in Psychology, English, and Digital Culture and New Media.
My education reflects my interest in both the creative and technical sides of design.
Interactive Systems Design is offered through the Computer Science Department and focuses on software development, interface design, and creating user-friendly digital experiences. Through this program, I've developed skills in programming, software design, computational thinking, and problem-solving, and understanding how people interact with technology. 
My Studio Art education allows me to explore the more expressive side of creativity. With a particular interest in digital art, I've gained experience in visual communication, composition, illustration, and experimenting with different artistic styles and techniques.
My minors further complement these interests. Psychology helps me better understand human behaviour and perception, English strengthens my communication and storytelling skills, and Digital Culture and New Media allows me to explore the relationship between creativity, technology, and contemporary digital experiences.
Together, these areas of study have shaped the way I approach design. I believe successful creative work should not only look good but also communicate clearly, serve a purpose, and consider the people interacting with it.

My Technical & Creative Experience

My interests extend across software development, web design, user interface design, digital media, and creative technology.
Through my education and personal projects, I've gained experience working with programming languages and technologies including Java, JavaFX, Python, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. Alongside my technical experience, I've developed a strong foundation in digital art and visual design using Canva, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator, and a variety of other creative applications. 

Beyond Design: My Love for Softball

While art and technology are important parts of my life, softball has played an equally significant role in shaping who I am.
I've been involved in the softball community for many years, and what began as a love for the sport has grown into a passion for coaching, and helping others develop their skills and confidence.
I currently serve as an Associate Coach and Student Group President with the University of Saskatchewan Women's Softball Team. In these roles, I contribute to practice planning, player development, team activities, fundraising, social media, and organizing skills camps.
I've also spent years coaching and instructing younger athletes, from introducing children to the fundamentals of softball to working with competitive players on more advanced skills and strategies.
In 2026, I became a Softball Saskatchewan Learning Facilitator, providing coach education and helping beginner softball coaches develop their knowledge and teaching skills.
One of the most rewarding parts of coaching is watching athletes grow, not only in their technical abilities but also in their confidence, independence, and understanding of teamwork.
Coaching has taught me the importance of communication, preparation, adaptability, patience, and attention to detail. It has also shown me how much thoughtful planning and a positive environment can impact someone's experience and development.

How Coaching Influences My Creative Work

At first glance, interactive systems design and coaching softball might seem like completely different worlds; I have found that many of the skills I use in coaching also influence how I approach creative projects.
Both require preparation, problem-solving, communication, and an understanding of the people you're working with.
As a coach, I consider how to adapt my approach to different athletes, communicate information clearly, and create an environment that supports growth. As a designer, I think about many of the same things: who the audience is, what they need, and how I can make an experience more effective and engaging.
Coaching has also helped me become comfortable taking initiative, working collaboratively, managing multiple responsibilities, and responding to unexpected challenges.
These experiences have shaped me into someone who values both creativity and structure. I love exploring new ideas, and thinking outside the box, but I also appreciate the organization, planning, and attention to detail needed to bring those ideas to life.

Always Creating, Always Learning

I consider myself someone with a wide range of interests and a constant curiosity about how things work.
I enjoy experimenting with new creative techniques, exploring different software, learning programming concepts, and taking on projects that push me outside my comfort zone. 
My interests don't fit neatly into one category, and I see that as a strength. I enjoy combining the analytical side of programming with the creativity of art and design, along with the communication and leadership skills I've developed through coaching.
As I continue developing my portfolio and professional experience, I'm excited to explore opportunities in software development, interactive systems, user experience, and other areas of technology. I'm equally open to discovering new interests and pursuing opportunities that challenge me to learn and grow.
Above all, I hope to create work that is thoughtful, functional, engaging, and meaningful.

Let's Connect!

I'm always interested in opportunities to collaborate, learn, and connect with others who share an interest in creativity, technology, and design.
Whether you're interested in working together, discussing a project, or simply connecting, I'd love to hear from you.

skostuk@outlook.com

Thanks for taking the time to learn a little more about me!
